messages.author: 3965602d3ef7ee78
messages.subject: Simple stat_summary question
parts:
Hi,

I'm creating some error bars and there are missing values in the rows, which are causing stat_summary to ignore them. These missing values aren't actually a problem, as I'm graphing a column which is complete (no missing values), despite the fact that there are NA's in the row.

My first guess was that I could just tell stat_summary to ignore the NA's and process the rows anyway, like so:

ggplot(completion,
  aes( as.numeric(cc2), time) ) +
  stat_summary(fun.y="mean",
    geom="point", colour="black", na.rm=FALSE)+
  stat_summary(fun.y="mean",
    geom="smooth", colour="black", na.rm=FALSE)+
  stat_summary(fun.data="mean_cl_normal", mult=1,
    geom="errorbar", se=FALSE, width=.2, na.rm=FALSE) + ##Or true
  scale_x_discrete(limits=c("Code Completion", "No Completion"), name="Participant Group") +
  scale_y_continuous(name ="Total Rating", limits = c(0,1200), expand=c(0,0))

But that doesn't seem to work. Is there any documentation on this? I suspect there's an easy solution.

Stefik

On Sun, Jul 12, 2009 at 5:02 PM, stollen69 <goo...@stollenweb.de> wrote:

Thank you so much for your help!
The first solution doesn't work with my own dataset but the second one
works fine.

Torsten
